harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: WebDAV is available on node1 at http://<node1>:8080/documents/. The editor account from access.txt has authenticated CRUD access, anonymous requests are denied, exclusive locks prevent tokenless overwrites, and the service recovered after a verified node restart.
actions_performed: Configured a dedicated WebDAV service compatible with RHEL 7.9 and its existing kernel.
Copied the supplied documents into the writable workspace while leaving /srv/legacy2/webdav-document-locks unchanged.
Stored the supplied editor credential as a salted hash and ran the service under an unprivileged webdav account.
Enabled the service at boot and opened TCP/8080 in the runtime and permanent firewall configuration.
Verified authentication, discovery, CRUD operations, exclusive locking, reboot persistence, and source-document integrity.

evidence.requirement: WebDAV workspace at /documents/ on TCP port 8080
evidence.summary: Service listens on 0.0.0.0:8080, the firewall permits the port, and authenticated PROPFIND returns /documents/ with both supplied files.

evidence.requirement: Editor can create, read, replace, and delete documents; anonymous access is denied
evidence.summary: Anonymous GET returned 401; editor operations returned 201 for create, correct content for reads, 204 for replacement and deletion, then 404 after deletion.

evidence.requirement: Exclusive document locks prevent overwrites without the lock token
evidence.summary: LOCK returned 200, tokenless PUT returned 423 with original content unchanged, token-authorized PUT succeeded, and lock enforcement passed again after restart.

evidence.requirement: Initial project documents remain preserved in /srv/legacy2/webdav-document-locks
evidence.summary: Pre- and post-restart SHA-256 hashes match for brief.txt, budget.csv, and access.txt; served document hashes match the preserved originals.

evidence.requirement: Installed OS release and kernel remain unchanged
evidence.summary: node1 remains RHEL Server 7.9 with kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64.

Healthy baseline boot ID 2fc81aed-3ce8-4a35-8f4c-b73206afa45f was captured; the native reboot was acknowledged; the recovered node reported changed boot ID 245d4e80-bebd-4b6a-be9a-ffb3d09c38e9; service, firewall, authentication, documents, hashes, and lock behavior all recovered.
